newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mostly up, mogas up $2 but CFDs flattening.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mostly up, mogas up $2 but CFDs flattening.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly firmer on Friday as gasoline and fuel climb but Brent crude held steady.
Brent CFDs were little changed for next week at around 34 cents a barrel under June after climbing 10 cents a barrel on Friday and flattening the near term contango.
The following two weeks talked around 33 cents under June, little changed from late Thursday.
Gasoline swaps firmed $2 a tonne, partially reversing a $3 fall on Thursday. May talked at $197 having dipped just below $195 on Thursday. June stayed $3.50 lower with July another $3.50 lower.
Gasoline crack spreads against Brent held steady at $4.10 a barrel and $3.10 for the third and fourth quarter this year.
Naphtha firmed $2.50 a tonne to $180.50 for May after losing ground on Thursday.

Heavy fuel firmed 50 cents a tonne to trade around $84 for May barges. The forward periods were pegged around $84.25 for July, $85 for July, $86 for the third quarter and $91.50 for the fourth quarter.
Low sulphur was valued around $90 for May but activity was thin.

Jet premiums were flat with May bid at $24.50 a tonne above the IPE after trading at that level last Thursday. The third and fourth quarters were little changed at $27.50 and $31.50 above the screen respectively.
